note: MEM-15. Not recall and not application: attribution. The same question is put to the same provider twice, once closed-book and once with what this vault's retrieval returned, and each answer is graded against a gold that was fixed before either call. Three fractions come out — lift (right with memory, wrong without), neutral, harm (right without memory, wrong with it). The harm fraction is the point. Cases are stratified the way arXiv 2605.29630 stratifies by discriminator tag: the `vault` stratum holds facts only this vault can supply, so a closed-book model cannot know them and lift is the only interesting outcome; the `world` stratum holds public facts verified on this machine by the command recorded in `gold_command`, chosen because their entity tokens collide with vault material that says something different about a different subject. That is this vault's honest analogue of the paper's pinned floor: we do not synthesise distractors, we pick questions whose collision already exists here and measure the degree. The `vault` stratum is not duplicated here — it is inherited from benchmark/vault-application-v1.json so the two stands cannot drift apart. Поправки 2026-08-28 после осмотра записанных ответов: (а) вопрос про busy_timeout переписан — 5000 мс это умолчание обёртки sqlite3.connect(timeout=5.0), а не самой SQLite, у которой 0, поэтому прежняя формулировка требовала неверного золота; (б) forbidden_tokens убраны из всех случаев — на этом корпусе механизм отверг четыре верных ответа (контрастная формулировка «True (то есть check=True не умолчание — умолчание check=False)», цитирование имени файла a.tar.gz, разбор «256 бит = 32 байта = 64 знака») и не отверг ни одного неверного. Механизм остаётся в коде и в тестах, корпус им не пользуется.
